---
title: "ESA toolbox"
subtitle: "Ecosystem service accounts for the EU27, from downloaded inputs to maps, workbooks and reports"
---

The ESA toolbox is a desktop tool that builds the ecosystem service accounts of the European Union for crop pollination, wood
provision and carbon sequestration, for the reporting years 2000, 2006, 2012, 2018 and 2024. It downloads its inputs from their
publishers, calculates the physical and monetary accounts, writes the maps and the results workbooks, and renders one report per
service that explains the method and presents the results of that run. Each service runs on its own, so a run can cover one, two
or all of them.

## What a run produces

Each service writes its products to its own folder, `outputs/<service>/`, with the workbook by NUTS level in `tables/`, the maps in
`maps/`, the report in HTML, PDF and Word in `report/`, and a record of the tool version, settings and timings in `run.json`.

| Service | Maps (100 m and 1 km) | Workbook (NUTS0, NUTS2, NUTS3) |
|:--|:----|:----|
| Crop pollination | Potential on all ecosystem types and on agroecosystems, demand, actual flow on all ecosystem types and on agroecosystems, unmet demand, value of the flow and of unmet demand | Potential, demand, actual flow and unmet demand in physical and monetary terms, and flow by ecosystem type |
| Carbon sequestration | Flow without offset, actual flow, missed flow, and the value of the actual and missed flows | The same quantities in physical and monetary terms |
| Wood provision | Actual flow, sustainable flow and overuse, in physical and monetary terms | The same quantities |

: Products of each service. {#tbl-products}

The reports carry no code. The method as implemented, with references to the code, is on the page of each service on this site.

## Install

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), then run:

```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/renatovargas/esa-toolbox
```

To work with exactly the versions of the libraries that made the published results, clone the repository and run the tool from
it, which installs the environment recorded in `uv.lock`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/renatovargas/esa-toolbox && cd esa-toolbox
uv sync --frozen
uv run esa doctor
```

GDAL comes inside the packages, so no system libraries are needed. The reports need [Quarto](https://quarto.org), which also
ships with Positron and RStudio. The tool finds those copies, and `QUARTO_PATH` points to any other.

## Quick start

Run `esa` with no arguments for a guided menu. It shows which inputs are in the store and which steps of each service are done,
and it asks what to run. Every choice prints the equivalent command.

```bash
esa                       # guided menu
esa doctor                # check the installation, disk, memory and Quarto
esa fetch carbon          # download the inputs of one service into the store
esa run carbon            # calculate, write maps, workbook and report
esa run pollination wood  # several services in one go
esa status                # what is done and what is out of date
```

A run resumes where it stopped, and it repeats only the steps whose code or settings changed. The full chain of the three
services takes about an hour on a desktop with 12 cores, most of it for the 100 m maps. See [Using the tool](site/usage.qmd)
for every command and setting.
